# Brief for the coach: the program amendment, 2 Nov 2026 draft

## Where things stand

The program in force is version 1, "Five compounds around the PT Tuesday", adopted 1 Nov 2026 as Joe's first program on this engine. It opened a training block the same day. The draft I worked on tonight (saved 2 Nov 2026, 21:08) is an amendment to it, not a redesign: if adopted, it becomes version 2, the block that opened on 1 Nov carries on unbroken, and the rotation stays in week A.

Nothing has been written yet. Everything below comes from a dry run, which validates the draft and shows what adopting would record without recording anything.

## What the program looks like (unchanged parts)

Six training days, Thursday off, a two-week rotation that differs only on Tuesday:

- Monday: overhead press, back and arms, 75-minute cap.
- Tuesday: the PT session at the gym. Week A is chest and back (estimated 6 hard sets chest, 6 lats, 3 biceps); week B is legs and core (6 quads, 4 glutes, 4 abs).
- Wednesday: pull-up volume and core, 75-minute cap, before the lunchtime run.
- Friday: strict pull-up test single, back squat and legs, 75-minute cap.
- Saturday: bench, back and arms, 90-minute cap.
- Sunday: deadlift and legs, 90-minute cap.
- Standing, not on the schedule: an optional conditioning circuit (Joe does it on a spare evening) and the daily hang.

The main lifts run as a top set at RPE 8 followed by back-off sets at 85 % of the top set: overhead press 1 × 5 then 4 × 6 (after warm-ups of 5 and 3); back squat 1 × 5 then 4 × 5 (warm-ups 5, 3, 2); bench 1 × 5 then 4 × 6 (warm-ups 8, 5, 3). Accessories run on double progression at RPE 8 in their stated ranges (chest-supported row 4 × 8–12, lateral raise 3 × 12–15, rear delt fly 3 × 12–15, Romanian deadlift 3 × 6–10, split squat 3 × 8–12, seated dumbbell press 3 × 8–12, calf raise 3 × 10–15, ab wheel 3 × 6–12, bent-over row 4 × 6–10, incline dumbbell bench 3 × 8–12, dip negatives 3 × 3–5, overhead triceps extension 3 × 10–15, lying leg raise 3 × 10–15). Wednesday's pull-up work: 2 activation sets of scapular pull-ups (6–8 at RPE 5), 3 sets of negatives at 2–4 reps, 4 sets of band pull-ups at 5–8 reps, 2 flexed-arm hangs of 20 s, 4 suitcase carries of 30 s. Friday opens with one strict pull-up single at RPE 10 as the weekly measure.

Volume targets: 10 hard sets per muscle per week; per lift, bench 5, overhead press 5, deadlift 4, squat 5 (pull-up changes below). Deload policy: at most 6 hard weeks in a block, then a light week cutting 40 % of the sets, keeping the load, capping everything at RPE 8, and testing the priority lifts.

## What the amendment changes

Four things. Each is what the dry run says would be recorded.

1. **The kettlebell swing finisher leaves Monday's lift.** Today it is the last line of the Monday session: 8 sets of 10 at RPE 7, 40 lb, 45 s rest, one set at the top of each minute. The dry run shows Monday's time estimate falling from 58 to 47 minutes against its 75-minute cap.

2. **A new optional conditioning session, swings every minute on the minute, sits beside Monday's lift in both rotation weeks.** Monday becomes two sessions, lift first, swings second. The swing session starts at 12 minutes of 12 swings a minute with the 40 lb bell (recorded in Hevy as 18.14 kg). When a session comes in at or under RPE 7, the next grows by 2 minutes, up to a 16-minute cap; the reps per minute can rise to a cap of 15. Being optional, it never counts against adherence; its done-count shows as a streak.

3. **The strict pull-up gets a real weekly volume target: 10 hard sets, with negatives and band pull-ups counting toward it.** Version 1 set the pull-up target at 1 (the single test rep) and had to carry an explanation for why that sat outside the 5–15 band. The engine now lets a lift count its variants, so negatives and band pull-ups add to the pull-up's weekly figure. As planned, Wednesday delivers 3 negatives plus 4 band sets, 7 counted sets, plus the Friday single: 8 sets against a target of 10, so expect the weekly card to show the pull-up a little under target until Joe adds sets or the variants grow. The old explanation is removed because the warning no longer fires. The variants count toward volume only: they never replace the strict pull-up on a line and are never tested.

4. **The deadlift's target of 4 stays, now with an explanation on record.** See the warning below.

Also recorded: the reason for the amendment (the engine update lets us drop two cutover workarounds: the pull-up's placeholder target and the swing finisher parked inside a lifting session). No defaults are filled by the engine; everything in the draft is authored. Start loads it would record: farmer's walk on Sunday 50 lb per hand (Hevy total 45.36 kg), swings 40 lb (18.14 kg) in both the new session and the standing circuit. Session estimates against caps: Monday 47 of 75, Wednesday 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90.

## Warnings on the dry run

Three remain. None blocks adoption (only violations do, and there are none).

**Deadlift volume target of 4 is below the 5–15 band for a priority lift.** This fires because the maintenance-phase band for a priority lift is 5–15 hard sets a week and the Sunday session plans exactly 4 (the top set and three back-offs). I left it with this explanation: Friday's Romanian deadlift carries the hinge pattern, the PT sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesday, and a target of 5 would show the deadlift under target every week the session is done as written. The warning would clear on its own if the target moved to 5 or more; with the explanation, it is recorded as a coaching judgement and shows as "left" rather than open.

**The strict pull-up single is on a "hold" scheme, which is outside the band for a priority lift.** Carried over from version 1 with its explanation: the single is the weekly measure while the max is 1; negatives and band pull-ups do the building under their own schemes; the strict line becomes working sets once the test rep passes about five. It would clear if the line moved to a progressing scheme, which we don't want yet.

**One Hevy routine has drifted from the plan in force for the week of 2 Nov.** The engine reports structural differences: the reps on sets 5, 6 and 7 of the first exercise, and the weights on sets 1, 2 and 3 of the second. It doesn't name the session in plain words, but the shape matches Monday's routine (7 sets of overhead press, then the chest-supported row), and Joe's Monday log fits: he pressed 8 reps on three back-offs where 6 were planned. This means Joe or the app edited the routine after it was pushed. It clears at the next weekly push, which rewrites the routine to the plan, or when the next week's plan carries an override matching the edit. Worth asking Joe whether he changed it on purpose, because the push will overwrite it.

One thing the dry run cannot see: the same-day stacking rule runs when a week's plan is drafted, not at adoption. Now that the swing session is a scheduled Monday session with an RPE target of 7 (the quality threshold), the weekly plan may suggest dropping it in any week where it falls within six hours of the Monday lift. Doing the swings in the evening with the lift in the morning, or accepting the suggestion in a heavy week, is the answer. The standing circuit was already flagged on 2 Nov for sharing Monday with the lift; that was left with the note that it is optional and Joe never stacks it on Monday.

## What Joe must agree to

- Version 2 is adopted as an amendment: same block (opened 1 Nov 2026), same rotation position (week A), no reset of anything.
- The swing finisher comes out of Monday's lift. If he wants swings on Monday, he does the separate 12-minute session, ideally several hours apart from the press.
- The pull-up's weekly volume is now scored at 10 hard sets counting negatives and band work; the card will likely show it one or two sets under at first.
- The deadlift stays at 4 planned hard sets with the reasoning on record.
- At the next weekly push, the drifted Hevy routine is rewritten to the plan (losing his edit unless we carry it), and a new routine is created for the swing session. Adoption itself writes nothing to Hevy.

## Context from the store that came back along the way

**Monday 2 Nov, as logged.** Overhead press 68 lb: 5 at RPE 7.5, then 6, 8, 8, 8 at RPE 6 (planned 4 × 6; he pushed the back-offs to 8). Chest-supported row 20 lb per hand: 6, 12, 12 at RPE 8, 7, 7.5 (planned 4 sets). Lateral raise 5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 6, 7.5. Rear delt fly 7.5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 7, 8. Swings 40 lb: 8 × 10, RPE 7 for six sets then 7.5, 7.5. The daily hang was logged with no figures.

**Pull-up history since September.** 27 Sep: band pull-ups 5, 5 at RPE 6. 26 Oct: strict single at RPE 10; negatives 2, 2 at RPE 8 and 9; band pull-ups 6, 5, 5 at RPE 8.5. 1 Nov: strict single at RPE 10; band pull-ups 6, 6, 5, 4 at RPE 8, 8.5, 9.5, 10. That last set of 4 at RPE 10 raised a "rep range missed" note: it went over the line, so the band load holds rather than progressing.

**Priority lifts (estimated one-rep max now; best logged set).** Bench 174.9; best 160.94 × 3 on 14 Apr 2026. Overhead press 85.15; best 93.0 × 5 on 10 Jul 2026. Deadlift: no current estimate; best 200.0 × 5 on 11 Apr 2026. Back squat 231.48; best 220.46 × 1 on 13 Oct 2026. Strict pull-up best 3 reps on 29 Mar 2026. Distance to the long-term targets: pull-up 2 reps short of 5; bench 0.32 of bodyweight short of 1.25×; overhead press 0.24 short of 0.75×; deadlift 0.9 short of 2×; squat 0.32 short of 1.5×. Phase is maintenance: target rate 0.0 % of bodyweight a week, observed −0.13 %, which the engine marks as not meeting the target; the phase ends on the coach's call.

**Warnings on the week of 2 Nov's plan** (the weekly plan, not the program):

- Stall streaks on overhead press, rear delt fly, band pull-ups, negatives, both calf raise lines, ab wheel, seated dumbbell press and bent-over row: three exposures in a row with no gain on each line's metric (load-based estimate for the press, reps at the rep-range for the others). These read imported history from before the engine. One exposure with a gain clears each; two more without may trigger the scheme's stall response.
- RPE ceiling unchecked on the goblet squat (load held at 20.25), chest-supported row (34), suitcase carry (4.25), seated dumbbell press (22.5) and split squat (4.25): no usable one-rep estimate exists to check the authored RPE, so the load simply holds. Logged reps with RPE on those lines clear it.
- Suitcase carry: the logged 0 is not a rack row, so the anchor uses 5. Logging a real load clears it.
- Back squat: the pinned 170.5 is more than one rack step above the anchor's 118. Left with the note that the anchor is a light home set, and the PT single of 100 kg on 13 Oct 2026 puts 170.5 at about 75 % of the estimated max, below what the scheme would have proposed.

The older plan draft dated 1 Nov still carries one blocking fault (a missing start load) and several warnings, but it is superseded by the plan in force for the week of 2 Nov and can be ignored.

first.text:
Practically, nothing about your sessions changes. Wednesday is still scapular pull-ups, three sets of negatives, four sets of band pull-ups, the hangs and the carries. Friday still opens with the one strict single at RPE 10 as the weekly test. The negatives and band work never replace the strict line and are never tested; the single stays the measure.

What changes is how the week is scored. Until now the pull-up's weekly figure counted only that one single, so the target had to be 1 and the week looked complete the moment you did the test rep, whether or not Wednesday happened. Now every hard set of negatives and band pull-ups counts toward the pull-up's weekly figure, against a target of 10. So three things follow:

- The weekly card actually tells you whether the pull-up got built that week. A lost Wednesday shows as the pull-up under target instead of being invisible.
- If it sits under target for three weeks out of four, that's the prompt to add sets or raise the band work, not to touch the strict single.
- The per-set rules are unchanged: last week's band set of 4 at RPE 10 means the band load holds rather than stepping up, same as before.

One thing I need to settle before we adopt. Earlier I counted the week at 11 sets including three band sets on Sunday; the latest read of the week as written gives 8: seven on Wednesday plus the Friday single, with no band work on Sunday. If 8 is right, a target of 10 would show the pull-up under every week you do exactly what's planned, which defeats the point. Two honest options: set the target to 8 to match the week as it is, or add two band sets to Sunday's deadlift day and keep 10. Given the pull-up is two reps from goal and the last set is reaching RPE 10, I'd lean toward adding the Sunday sets. I'll confirm the count and come back with the corrected numbers before anything is recorded. Which way do you want to go?
